skipSemantics: May-skip, not must-skip: a listed test that runs and passes on a machine where its precondition holds is green. Matching is exact on the pre-'(' portion of the TRX result testName (xunit theory rows serialize with arguments, e.g. Class.Method(x: 1)); a name with no parens matches whole. Anchor is the TRX result list, never Counters arithmetic.
admissionRule: allowedSkips is not a quarantine list. A test may be listed only when its precondition is a property of the machine or OS that cannot be satisfied by configuration during a contract run, and its change names the machine class where it executes. Two named PERMANENT BANS apply: (1) CcpClient.Tests.DataRootOverrideTests.DefaultSettingsPath_EnvUnset_IsThePlatformDefault must never be allowed to skip because a process-wide CCP_DATA_ROOT override makes the floor vacuous; (2) CcpClient.Tests.ChaosTunnelLoopbackTests.Logging_RouteClassesOnly_NeverFilenameOrQuery must be fixed at the source, never quarantined.
bumpRule: Bump total only in the same commit as the test change that moves the count, with the reason recorded here. Never widen, disable, or special-case a check to make a step pass. Adding a name to allowedSkips requires the admission rule above and the machine class where it executes.
lastMovedBy: Merged lane/unbounded-joins: a source guard for the two wait shapes that carry NO timing literal and were therefore invisible to the wall-clock guard and to review - (a) an unbounded join and (b) a timeout budget injected by name and then waited on. +8 in CcpClient.Tests, 0 headless. Seven are the lane's own facts (each shape flagged from a three-line string, so the inversion is a test rather than a manual step, plus the deferral to TestTimingGuardTests.ForbiddenTokens so no site is pinned twice). The eighth is the fact an independent review demanded: the guard originally matched Task.WhenAll/WaitAll and awaited signals but NOT a bare .Wait()/.WaitOne()/.GetAwaiter().GetResult(), which is the very shape whose failure mode - the run dying by outer kill with no failing test name - the guard's own docstring names as its reason to exist. That omission produced a severity INVERSION against its sibling: TestTimingGuardTests bans .Wait(TimeSpan, so a BOUNDED five-second wait needed a marker and a pin while the UNBOUNDED form needed nothing, and the lane had marked an awaited signal at AsyncLifecycleTests.cs:184 while leaving an unbounded ManualResetEventSlim.Wait() five lines above it in the same lambda. The shape is now covered (argument-less by construction, so the timed forms still belong to the wall-clock guard), obj/ is excluded from both walks so a generated entry point cannot red it, and all 23 live sites are dispositioned: ONE bounded (InputWindowProbe.cs:613, the only real defect found - a Win32 throw on that thread would have hung the whole run forever) and 22 pinned with reasons, each either a wedge that IS the subject or a sync-over-async bridge whose target returns Task.CompletedTask on the calling thread. CcpClient.Tests 2665 to 2673, CcpClient.HeadlessTests unchanged at 154.
